D1.interpretation: Counts source rows (one per LCA case) where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring, so titles like 'Senior Data Analyst' count; no other title classes added), and the recorded worksite state is Massachusetts (WORKSITE_STATE 'MA'). Employers are grouped by EMPLOYER_NAME exactly as filed; spelling or punctuation variants of the same company are not merged. Results are ranked by case count descending, then employer name alphabetically, and limited to the top ten as the question asks.
D1.sql: SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME AS employer_name, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_STATE)) IN ('MA', 'MASSACHUSETTS') GROUP BY EMPLOYER_NAME ORDER BY cases DESC, employer_name ASC LIMIT 10
D1.rows_sql: WITH top_employers AS (SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_STATE)) IN ('MA', 'MASSACHUSETTS') GROUP BY EMPLOYER_NAME ORDER BY cases DESC, EMPLOYER_NAME ASC LIMIT 10) SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_STATE)) IN ('MA', 'MASSACHUSETTS') AND EMPLOYER_NAME IN (SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME FROM top_employers) ORDER BY EMPLOYER_NAME ASC, sheet_row ASC
D1.limits: Top ten only, as requested; if employers tie at tenth place, the alphabetical tie breaker decides which are shown and tied employers may be left out. Only the one recorded worksite city/state per case is used; additional worksites are not in the data. Employer names are not normalized, so one company filing under variant names is split. A certified LCA is not a visa approval, job offer, hire, or promise of future sponsorship.

D2.interpretation: Counts source rows (one per LCA case) where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added), and the single recorded worksite is Boston, MA (WORKSITE_CITY 'Boston' and WORKSITE_STATE 'MA', compared case-insensitively after trimming). Source rows are counted, not distinct case numbers.
D2.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_CITY)) = 'BOSTON' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_STATE)) IN ('MA', 'MASSACHUSETTS')
D2.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_CITY)) = 'BOSTON' AND UPPER(TRIM(WORKSITE_STATE)) IN ('MA', 'MASSACHUSETTS') ORDER BY sheet_row ASC
D2.limits: The workbook records one worksite city/state pair per case plus a total worksite count, but not every additional worksite. Cases whose recorded worksite is elsewhere but which list Boston as a secondary worksite cannot be detected, so this counts only cases whose recorded worksite is Boston, MA. Neighborhood or variant spellings (e.g., a Boston suburb name) are not included. A certified LCA is not a visa approval, job offer, or hire.

D3.interpretation: Counts source rows (one per LCA case) where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', and JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added). Cases are grouped by the recorded worksite city and state pair exactly as filed (WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE), so same-named cities in different states stay separate. Ranked by case count descending, then city and state alphabetically, limited to ten as the question asks.
D3.sql: SELECT WORKSITE_CITY AS city, WORKSITE_STATE AS state, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE ORDER BY cases DESC, city ASC, state ASC LIMIT 10
D3.rows_sql: WITH top_cities AS (SELECT WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE ORDER BY cases DESC, WORKSITE_CITY ASC, WORKSITE_STATE ASC LIMIT 10) SELECT l.sheet_row, l.CASE_NUMBER, l.CASE_STATUS, l.VISA_CLASS, l.EMPLOYER_NAME, l.JOB_TITLE, l.WORKSITE_CITY, l.WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca l JOIN top_cities t ON l.WORKSITE_CITY IS t.WORKSITE_CITY AND l.WORKSITE_STATE IS t.WORKSITE_STATE WHERE TRIM(l.CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(l.VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(l.JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' ORDER BY l.WORKSITE_STATE ASC, l.WORKSITE_CITY ASC, l.sheet_row ASC
D3.limits: Top ten only, as requested; ties at tenth place are broken alphabetically and tied cities may be left out. Only the one recorded worksite per case is used; additional worksites are not in the data. City names are grouped as filed, so case or spelling variants of the same city are counted separately. A certified LCA is not a visa approval, job offer, or hire.

D4.interpretation: Uses source rows where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', and JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added). 'Offered annual base wage' is taken as WAGE_RATE_OF_PAY_FROM, the lower bound of the filed base-wage range (not total compensation), restricted to rows whose WAGE_UNIT_OF_PAY is 'Year' with a non-blank wage; hourly, weekly, bi-weekly, and monthly rows are excluded rather than annualized, because no hours/weeks convention is given. The wage text is cast to a number after stripping '$' and commas. Grouped by the recorded WORKSITE_STATE as filed. Median is the middle value, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even. 'cases' is the number of rows used for that state's median.
D4.sql: WITH w AS (SELECT WORKSITE_STATE AS state, CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(WAGE_RATE_OF_PAY_FROM), '$', ''), ',', '') AS REAL) AS wage FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND LOWER(TRIM(WAGE_UNIT_OF_PAY)) = 'year' AND TRIM(COALESCE(WAGE_RATE_OF_PAY_FROM, '')) <> ''), ranked AS (SELECT state, wage, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY wage) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY state) AS n FROM w) SELECT state, AVG(wage) AS median_usd, MAX(n) AS cases FROM ranked WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY state ORDER BY state ASC
D4.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND LOWER(TRIM(WAGE_UNIT_OF_PAY)) = 'year' AND TRIM(COALESCE(WAGE_RATE_OF_PAY_FROM, '')) <> '' ORDER BY WORKSITE_STATE ASC, sheet_row ASC
D4.limits: Medians use the lower bound of the filed base-wage range only, not WAGE_RATE_OF_PAY_TO, and are not total compensation. Rows filed in non-annual units are excluded, not converted; annualizing them would need a stated hours/weeks convention (e.g., 2080 hours/year) and could change the result. No minimum sample size is applied, so states with one or two cases show a median from very few filings. State is the single recorded worksite state. Filed wages are not actual pay, and a certified LCA is not a visa approval or hire.

D5.interpretation: Counts source rows where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', and JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added). Grouped by PW_WAGE_LEVEL after trimming; NULL and empty values are combined into one row labeled '(blank)'. Ordered by wage level.
D5.sql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(PW_WAGE_LEVEL), ''), '(blank)') AS wage_level, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY wage_level ORDER BY wage_level ASC
D5.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' ORDER BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(PW_WAGE_LEVEL), ''), '(blank)') ASC, sheet_row ASC
D5.limits: '(blank)' combines NULL and empty-string wage levels; it is a label, not a DOL value. A blank level means the field was not populated in the workbook (e.g., a wage source without a level), not that the case had no prevailing wage. A certified LCA is not a visa approval or hire.

D6.interpretation: Counts source rows where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', PW_WAGE_LEVEL is 'I' (after trimming), and JOB_TITLE matches one of the three named title classes by case-insensitive substring: 'data analyst', 'business analyst', or 'bi analyst'. 'Business intelligence analyst' is treated as the spelled-out form of BI Analyst and included; no other title classes are added. Employers are grouped by EMPLOYER_NAME exactly as filed (variants not merged). Every matching employer is returned, no LIMIT, ranked by case count descending then employer name alphabetically.
D6.sql: SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME AS employer_name, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND TRIM(PW_WAGE_LEVEL) = 'I' AND (LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%bi analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business intelligence analyst%') GROUP BY EMPLOYER_NAME ORDER BY cases DESC, employer_name ASC
D6.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND TRIM(PW_WAGE_LEVEL) = 'I' AND (LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%bi analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business intelligence analyst%') ORDER BY EMPLOYER_NAME ASC, sheet_row ASC
D6.limits: All matching employers are returned; the list is not truncated. Including 'business intelligence analyst' is a stated choice; a literal 'BI Analyst'-only match would drop spelled-out titles and could change the list. Titles are matched by substring, so seniority or qualifier variants (e.g., 'Senior Business Analyst') are included even at Level I. Employer names are not normalized. Level I is the prevailing-wage level on the filing, not a statement about the worker's experience, and a certified LCA is not a visa approval, job offer, or hire.

D7.interpretation: Counts source rows where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', EMPLOYER_NAME contains 'capgemini america' (case-insensitive substring, so suffixes like ', Inc.' match; TRADE_NAME_DBA is not used), and JOB_TITLE matches one of the three named title classes by case-insensitive substring: 'data analyst', 'business analyst', or 'bi analyst' ('business intelligence analyst' included as the spelled-out form of BI Analyst; no other classes added). Grouped by JOB_TITLE exactly as filed. Every matching title is returned, ranked by case count descending then title alphabetically. Zero rows means no such certified filings in this quarter's data.
D7.sql: SELECT JOB_TITLE AS job_title, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(EMPLOYER_NAME) LIKE '%capgemini america%' AND (LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%bi analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business intelligence analyst%') GROUP BY JOB_TITLE ORDER BY cases DESC, job_title ASC
D7.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(EMPLOYER_NAME) LIKE '%capgemini america%' AND (LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%bi analyst%' OR LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%business intelligence analyst%') ORDER BY JOB_TITLE ASC, sheet_row ASC
D7.limits: Covers only the FY2026 Q3 workbook. The employer match is a name substring; the matched EMPLOYER_NAME values are visible in the rows so the user can confirm they are the intended entity, and other Capgemini entities (e.g., a name without 'America') are excluded. Titles are grouped as filed, so case or punctuation variants of one title appear separately. Past certified LCAs do not guarantee or predict that Capgemini will sponsor anyone in the future, and an LCA is not a visa approval or hire.

D8.interpretation: Counts source rows where VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B' and SOC_CODE begins with '15-2051' (trimmed prefix match, so formats like '15-2051.00' are included). No case-status filter is applied because the question does not ask for one, so all statuses (Certified, Certified - Withdrawn, Withdrawn, Denied) are counted. Grouped by JOB_TITLE exactly as filed, ranked by case count descending then title alphabetically, limited to ten as the output shape asks.
D8.sql: SELECT JOB_TITLE AS job_title, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND TRIM(SOC_CODE) LIKE '15-2051%' GROUP BY JOB_TITLE ORDER BY cases DESC, job_title ASC LIMIT 10
D8.rows_sql: WITH top_titles AS (SELECT JOB_TITLE, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND TRIM(SOC_CODE) LIKE '15-2051%' GROUP BY JOB_TITLE ORDER BY cases DESC, JOB_TITLE ASC LIMIT 10) SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND TRIM(SOC_CODE) LIKE '15-2051%' AND JOB_TITLE IN (SELECT JOB_TITLE FROM top_titles) ORDER BY JOB_TITLE ASC, sheet_row ASC
D8.limits: Top ten only; ties at tenth place are broken alphabetically and tied titles may be left out. All case statuses are included; restricting to 'Certified' would change the counts. The '15-2051' prefix also includes any O*NET detail codes under it (e.g., '15-2051.01' Business Intelligence Analysts, '15-2051.02' Clinical Data Managers) if they appear in the data; an exact '15-2051'/'15-2051.00' match would exclude them. Titles are grouped as filed, so case or punctuation variants are counted separately. SOC coding is the employer's classification.

D9.interpretation: Counts source rows where CASE_STATUS is exactly 'Certified' (not 'Certified - Withdrawn'), VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B', and JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added). Month is the first seven characters (YYYY-MM) of the ISO DECISION_DATE. One row per month present, in month order.
D9.sql: SELECT SUBSTR(DECISION_DATE, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC
D9.rows_sql: SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' ORDER BY SUBSTR(DECISION_DATE, 1, 7) ASC, sheet_row ASC
D9.limits: The data is one fiscal quarter (FY2026 Q3), so only months with decisions in that file appear; months with zero cases are not listed. A missing DECISION_DATE would show as a NULL month. Decision month is when DOL decided the LCA, not a hire or start date, and a certified LCA is not a visa approval.

D10.interpretation: 'Certified and then withdrawn' is read as CASE_STATUS exactly 'Certified - Withdrawn' (distinct from 'Certified' and from plain 'Withdrawn', which are excluded). Also VISA_CLASS is exactly 'H-1B' and JOB_TITLE contains 'data analyst' (case-insensitive substring; no other title classes added). Source rows are counted; employers are grouped by EMPLOYER_NAME exactly as filed (variants not merged). Ranked by case count descending then employer name alphabetically, limited to ten as the output shape asks.
D10.sql: SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME AS employer_name, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified - Withdrawn' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY EMPLOYER_NAME ORDER BY cases DESC, employer_name ASC LIMIT 10
D10.rows_sql: WITH top_employers AS (SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME, COUNT(*) AS cases FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified - Withdrawn' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' GROUP BY EMPLOYER_NAME ORDER BY cases DESC, EMPLOYER_NAME ASC LIMIT 10) SELECT sheet_row, CASE_NUMBER, CASE_STATUS, VISA_CLASS, EMPLOYER_NAME, JOB_TITLE, WORKSITE_CITY, WORKSITE_STATE FROM lca WHERE TRIM(CASE_STATUS) = 'Certified - Withdrawn' AND TRIM(VISA_CLASS) = 'H-1B' AND LOWER(JOB_TITLE) LIKE '%data analyst%' AND EMPLOYER_NAME IN (SELECT EMPLOYER_NAME FROM top_employers) ORDER BY EMPLOYER_NAME ASC, sheet_row ASC
D10.limits: Top ten only; ties at tenth place are broken alphabetically and tied employers may be left out. Plain 'Withdrawn' cases (withdrawn before certification) are not included. The data does not say why an LCA was withdrawn, so this says nothing about whether a job was cancelled, filled, or refiled. Employer names are not normalized.
